question: Where do a tier's host and model live in `.sober/config.jsonc` — one string, a host-and-model pair, or a tier→host table beside a host→model table?

options.label: One command line per tier: `dispatch.tiers.high = "claude --model claude-fable-5-1"`
options.reason: It is the shape `dispatch.host` already has. `adapterFor` finds the adapter, `hostCommand` splits it, and the model flag is typed in the host's own spelling — no new syntax, no new adapter row. A tier is a `dispatch.host` with a name.
options.costLater: SOBER cannot read the model back out of the string, so the record, `sober status` and the dashboard show `opencode --model minimax/m3-free` as one blob. Nothing validates that the model exists on that host, and each host's flag spelling (`--model`, `-m`, `provider/model`) is the user's to get right.

options.label: A pair per tier: `dispatch.tiers.high = { host: "claude", model: "claude-fable-5-1" }`
options.reason: The model is a field SOBER can show on its own, record on its own, and validate against the host. `sober status` says "high · claude · fable-5.1" without parsing a shell string.
options.costLater: A fifth row in the adapter table — how each host spells its model flag — read off all four CLIs and recorded (BUILD-PLAN §6 forbids writing it from memory). OpenCode wants `provider/model`, so the field is not the same string on every host. And `dispatch.host` keeps carrying the model inside the command line, so the same fact lives in two shapes until `dispatch.host` is retired.

options.label: Two tables: `dispatch.tiers.<tier> = "<host>"` beside `dispatch.models.<host>.<tier>`
options.reason: Keeps `a-model-per-tier-per-host-in-the-config` exactly as titled and adds one word per tier on top. Moving a tier between hosts is a one-word edit; every host keeps its own model names.
options.costLater: Two lookups to learn what runs a node, and a new error when a tier points at a host whose model table has no row for it. The widest config of the three, and the one a reader has to trace by hand.
